title: Coming soon on ZDF: Mission Pinguin
text:
Carsten Behrendt, who joined the expedition, during the editing of the documentary.
From the Drake Passage to the penguin colonies of the Danger Islands, a new ZDF documentary brings our Antarctic expedition to the screen.
In Mission Pinguin – Mit dem Segelboot in die Antarktis, reporter Carsten Behrendt follows the scientists and sailors aboard Malizia Explorer, with Boris Herrmann. The approximately 43-minute film offers an insight into Antarctic field research, wildlife, and the challenges of reaching these remote islands.

title: Our Mission
text:
ANTARCTIC WILDLIFE PROTECTION

Science under sail. Protection through knowledge.
Our mission is to build the scientific foundation for protecting Antarctica’s most important wildlife habitats.
Starting in 2027/28, our international team will return every two years to the Antarctic Peninsula and the Danger Islands aboard Malizia Explorer. By tracking penguins and other seabirds, monitoring their colonies, and uncovering past ecosystem change, we will identify the places these animals depend on—and build the long-term evidence needed to guide their protection.

title: The Team
text:
Simeon Lisovski
Scientific Lead · Polar Ecology & Conservation
Simeon is a researcher at the Alfred Wegener Institute and the Leibnitz Insitute for Zoo and Wildlife Research specialising in polar biology and seabird ecology. He studies how environmental change affects wildlife, animal movements, and ecosystem health, with Antarctic fieldwork on Adélie penguins, skuas, and southern giant petrels. His research also examines how pathogens reach Antarctica and how avian influenza circulates among seabirds. For Antarctic Wildlife Protection, he leads the scientific programme, linking seabird tracking and colony monitoring to habitat conservation.
Meet Simeon at AWI ↗

title: The Team
text:
Esther Horvath
Photography & Science Communication
Esther is a documentary and science photographer whose work brings polar research and the people behind it into public view. Since 2015, she has documented scientific expeditions in the polar regions, including the MOSAiC expedition. Her photography received a World Press Photo award in 2020. Through photographs and stories, she connects audiences with Antarctic wildlife, the realities of field research, and the importance of protecting these environments.
Website ↗ · Instagram ↗

title: The Team
text:
Team Malizia
Research Platform, Outreach & Ocean Education
Boris Herrmann and his Team Malizia connects offshore sailing with ocean science, education, and climate action. The team contributes the research sailing vessel Malizia Explorer, alongside its communication and education activities. Its My Ocean Challenge programme brings ocean and climate science to young people—including live connections between classrooms and Antarctic expeditions. Together, these contributions help researchers reach remote habitats and bring the expedition’s discoveries to audiences beyond the scientific community.

title: Become a Partner
text:
Adélie penguins on the ice with Malizia Explorer anchored nearby.




SCIENCE · SAILING · SHARED PURPOSE


Partnerships help make our research possible—from reaching remote Antarctic habitats to sharing what we discover.
We welcome conversations with individuals, foundations, companies, and organisations who would like to contribute. Support can take many forms: funding, equipment, practical expertise, or helping our findings reach new audiences.
Start a conversation

title: Become a Partner
section: Different ways to make a difference
text:
Different ways to make a difference
There is no single way to become involved. Together, we can explore where your interests and our research needs meet.


Expeditions & fieldwork
Help make research voyages possible through support for transport, expedition logistics, and the time needed to work in remote Antarctic habitats.


Scientific equipment & research
Contribute towards tracking devices, field instruments, laboratory analyses, or tools that help us understand wildlife and its habitats.


Knowledge & practical expertise
Bring skills, services, or technical support—from equipment development and field logistics to data analysis and interpretation.


Education & communication
Help bring Antarctic research into classrooms and share its discoveries through photography, films, exhibitions, and public engagement.

title: Become a Partner
text:
Small devices. A wider understanding.
Tracking devices help reveal where penguins and other seabirds find food—and which marine habitats they depend on.
Supporting equipment is one practical way to contribute to this work. Combined with repeated field observations and colony monitoring, these measurements help build the evidence needed to guide habitat protection.
